strengths: Addresses important problem combining nonlinearity with local sparsity in functional data, with compelling real-world motivation (ECG, neuroimaging).
Novel integration of B-spline expansions, Bayesian DNNs, and structured spike-and-slab priors for interpretable region selection.
Strong theoretical contributions: approximation error bounds (Theorem 5.4), posterior consistency (Theorem 5.7), and selection consistency (Theorem 5.9) with clear assumptions.
Comprehensive empirical evaluation: diverse simulations varying multiple factors, four real datasets, multiple baselines, and both prediction and region identification metrics.
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameter specifications, promised code, dataset links, and preprocessing details.
Clear presentation of motivation, methodology, and results with informative visualizations including PIP plots demonstrating interpretability.
weaknesses: Significant gap between Bayesian framing and practical use: MAP estimation rather than full Bayesian inference; plug-in PIPs are asymptotic approximations with unclear finite-sample reliability; multiple random restarts (R=5) suggest optimization challenges.
Region identification precision is consistently low (ECG=0.464, Tecator=0.204) despite high recall, severely limiting interpretability utility—the key motivation for region selection.

Theory-practice gap: Theorem 5.7 requires specific Hₙ-sₙ relationships and hyperparameter rates (Assumption 5.5) that differ substantially from practical defaults; Assumption 5.8 (identifiability) is abstract and hard to verify.
Single-index model assumption (Eq. 1) is restrictive; no discussion of robustness when assumption is violated or guidance on model validation.
Prediction improvements are often modest (RMSE differences <5%) and sometimes marginal (Table 2), questioning whether methodological complexity is justified.

Practical considerations largely unaddressed: no computational cost analysis, no failure mode discussion, limited guidance on hyperparameter selection (Jₙ, network architecture) beyond defaults, scalability to high-dimensional functional inputs unclear.

Region evaluation limitations: only silver-standard annotations (not gold-standard) for ECG/Tecator; no region metrics for Bike/IHPC; limited comparison with methods designed for region selection (FNN, AdaFNN don't perform selection).
Algorithm 1 (critical for reproducibility) relegated to appendix; hyperparameter sensitivity analysis absent; no honest discussion of method limitations and when it is/isn't recommended.

strengths: First theoretical guarantees for Bayesian deep functional models: rigorous approximation error bounds, posterior consistency, and selection consistency with complete proofs
Well-motivated problem addressing genuine gap between linear interpretable methods and nonlinear black-box approaches; excellent ECG application motivation
Methodologically elegant: spike-and-slab priors on first-layer weight columns combined with flexible deeper layers; clever integration of B-spline localization with DNN flexibility

Comprehensive experimental validation: 24 simulation scenarios with 100 replicates each, 4 real-world datasets, 5 baselines, extensive supplementary analysis including robustness to model misspecification and heavy-tailed errors

Strong empirical results: consistent superiority under nonlinear relationships; better recall-precision balance than baselines; posterior inclusion probabilities provide interpretable uncertainty quantification
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithm, hyperparameter specifications, runtime analysis, stability assessment (Appendix A.7), extensive supplementary materials promised to be available

Honest treatment of limitations: clearly acknowledged constraints on single functional predictor, single projection direction, B-spline dependency, and appropriately discussed when assumptions may fail
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: Assumptions 5.5-5.6 specify complex hyperparameter rates depending on unknown problem-dependent quantities; practical algorithm uses fixed defaults not tuned to theoretical requirements; no empirical validation that theoretical contraction rates manifest in finite samples

Critical B-spline resolution dependency: choice of J_n requires careful tuning; evidence-based selection achieves only 44.1% top-3 in candidate set and 73.5% within 15% of oracle F1; no principled solution beyond validation set; larger J_n leads to region fragmentation

Modest real-data region selection quality: precision remains low (ECG 0.464, Tecator 0.204) despite high recall; selected regions wider than silver-standard annotations; clinical validation that identified regions are actionable missing; region interpretation depends on domain knowledge

Restrictive model scope: single functional predictor assumption; single projection direction per region; cannot extend directly to multiple functional inputs or classification problems; while honestly acknowledged, significantly limits applicability

Identifiability assumption (5.8) can be violated under strong collinearity: structural difference condition ρ_n(4ε_n) → 0 may not hold; paper acknowledges this but leaves unclear when assumption holds in practice

MAP-based inference not fully justified: cited literature supports MAP PIPs but exact full Bayesian posterior marginals would be preferable; computational cost/benefit analysis of MAP vs. full sampling missing; stability analysis (Appendix A.7) limited to fixed scenarios
Simulation data generated from assumed single-index model: validates method within model class but does not challenge assumptions; robustness experiments (FGAM, heavy-tailed) relegated to appendices
